why_how.text: Drivers and bicyclists must obey official road signs and traffic signals unless an officer or emergency worker directs otherwise.
The handbook describes seven basic sign shapes and recommends recognizing shape and color early enough to respond from a distance.
A tall rectangular sign generally gives a regulatory instruction that must be obeyed like a traffic law.
A wide rectangular sign generally provides guidance such as a destination, direction or special information.
A diamond-shaped warning sign identifies an actual or possible hazard on or beside the road; the described standard warning colors are yellow with black words or symbols.
An eight-sided sign means stop. Make a complete stop at the marked stop line, or before the near-side crosswalk when there is no line.
If a stop-controlled approach has neither a stop line nor a crosswalk, stop where approaching traffic can best be observed.

why_how.text: After stopping, remain stopped for pedestrians crossing the side you will travel on and yield to traffic close enough to create a conflict before moving again.
A round warning sign indicates a railroad crossing ahead. Slow, look, listen and prepare to stop; opening a window may help you hear a train.
At a rail crossing, stop for an approaching train rather than trying to judge whether you can beat it. Passing at the crossing is prohibited.
A triangular yield sign requires a speed appropriate for conditions and a stop when needed, at the marked line if one is present.
After slowing or stopping at a yield sign, give way to vehicles in the intersection or approaching closely on the intersecting road.

why_how.text: Regulatory signs specify permitted and prohibited actions, and bicyclists as well as other drivers must obey them.
A red circle crossed diagonally from its upper-left side toward its lower-right side means that the pictured action is prohibited.
The wrong-way warning identifies an approach where travel in your present direction onto the one-way road or ramp is forbidden.
The one-way instruction permits travel only in the direction indicated by its arrow.
The do-not-enter meaning applies when traffic on the one-way road is coming toward your approach; do not continue onto that road.
A no-U-turn restriction forbids reversing direction through a U-turn at that intersection.
A no-right-turn restriction prohibits turning right at that intersection.
